description:
Give library unit tests one shared fixture for canonical issue ids, so tests keep compiling and passing once issue ids are validated.

## Background

Unit tests under `crates/jit/src` build issues, events, gate runs and leases with non-UUID ids such as `"dep1"` or `"task-1"` in about 25 files. The heaviest are `domain/queries.rs` (27 lines), `storage/claim_coordinator.rs` (16), `output.rs` (15), `graph/hierarchy.rs` (9), `repository_state/mutation.rs` (8), `main.rs` (7), `commands/gate_check.rs` (7), `validation/graph.rs` (6), `storage/repository_state_store_tests.rs` (6), `storage/gate_runs.rs` (6) and `commands/worktree.rs` (6); the others are listed in the footprint. Rustdoc examples with non-UUID ids sit at `domain/queries.rs:114-116,416-430`, `graph/hierarchy.rs:110-116` and `storage/claim_coordinator.rs:63-70`. Shared fixtures live in `test_utils.rs`, compiled under `test` or the `test-support` feature (`lib.rs:20`), so integration suites can reach them too.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `test_utils` provides one fixture that deterministically returns a distinct canonical issue id, typed as `IssueId`, for each distinct seed.
- [hard] REQ-02: No unit test or rustdoc example under `crates/jit/src` that builds an issue, an issue summary, a gate-run result, an event or a lease uses a non-UUID issue id, and no test assigns an issue id from a string conversion (`to_string`, `into`, `format!`). Each takes its id from the fixture or from a generated id.
- [hard] REQ-03: Graph test nodes that do not model issues keep their own ids.
- [hard] REQ-04: A test that asserted a literal id asserts the relationship it cares about instead, such as id equality or the short id of a given id.
title: Library unit tests take canonical issue ids from one fixture
